page: Amazon Web Services m2.xlarge is a second-generation general-purpose server instance utilizing the Xen hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2665 0 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.4 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs, with 1 thread per core. It includes 17.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.55 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 420 GB HDD, and there is no GPU acceleration.

Performance benchmarks place the m2.xlarge in the lower tiers of modern cloud compute capabilities. In CPU-focused tests, the instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1310.39 (bottom 25%) and a multi-core score of 1719.98 (bottom 10%). Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block transfers measuring 13.55 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 11.48 GB/sec. The lack of modern instruction sets, such as AVX, AVX-512, and AES-NI, limits its efficiency in cryptographic and vector-heavy workloads, as reflected in its Passmark CPU encryption score of 265.82.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m2.xlarge offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of over 8 GB per core, which may benefit legacy applications requiring moderate memory footprints without high CPU demands. However, its reliance on older HDD local storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps limits its suitability for high-throughput database or real-time web serving tasks. This instance is best suited for legacy general-purpose workloads, basic file hosting, or low-intensity background processing that does not require modern instruction sets or high-speed networking.
